newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-LOFTON GOES 5-FOR-5 TO LEAD BRAVES IN POUNDING OF REDS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-LOFTON GOES 5-FOR-5 TO LEAD BRAVES IN POUNDING OF REDS.

text.p: Kenny Lofton went 5-for-5 and tied a team record with five runs scored as the Atlanta Braves pounded the Cincinnati Reds 15-5 Monday.
Lofton, who raised his average to .393, tied the Atlanta mark set by Lonnie Smith, who scored five times on May 6, 1989.
Michael Tucker went 3-for-6 with a career-high four RBI for the Braves, who have won nine of their last 10 games. Tucker raised his average to .372.
"When we put the ball in play anything can happen," Lofton said. "Pitchers are always worried about myself and Michael."

"Last year I learned to be more patient," Tucker said. "Pitchers were trying to make me get myself out. I started waiting for the pitch that I could hit. I'm getting good hacks and being patient and it's paying off for us."
Denny Neagle (1-0) allowed five runs and six hits over 5 2/3 innings to pick up his first victory of the season. Four relievers combined to hold the Reds scoreless on three hits.

Atlanta had 19 hits and every position player had at least two except for shortstop Jeff Blauser, who entered the game hitting a league-leading .450. Javier Lopez had three hits, including a grand slam in a five-run seventh inning.
"It was one of those nights where everything we hit hard was in and everything we hit soft was in," Atlanta manager Bobby Cox said.
"Kenny Lofton's been sensational. It doesn't surprise me if he gets a hit every time up."
Pete Schourek (0-2) was tagged for six hits and five runs, four earned, in 3 2/3 innings. He fell to 2-6 lifetime against Atlanta.
Deion Sanders had two hits and tied the Reds' club record with four stolen bases, last done by Eric Davis on April 24, 1986.

In Colorado, Andres Galarraga's two-run single in the sixth inning snapped a tie and keyed a three-run uprising as the Rockies posted a 10-8 victory over the Montreal Expos, their eighth win in nine games.
Larry Walker added three hits and three RBI for the Rockies, who scored 10 or more runs for the fifth time in 11 games this season. Colorado also improved to 5-1 against Montreal.

Jerry DiPoto (1-0) picked up the win by recording the final two outs of the sixth inning. He allowed one run and two hits in 1 1/3 innings overall. Bruce Ruffin struck out three in the ninth around a two-out double by Mark Grudzielanek for his second save.

Everett Stull (0-1), making his major-league debut, took the loss, allowing three runs and five hits in two innings. Montreal scored 24 runs in the three-game series, but allowed 22 in the two losses.
Shane Andrews homered for Montreal while Vinny Castilla got his sixth of the season for Colorado.
In St. Louis, pinch-hitter Bill Spiers stroked a two-run double in the 10th inning as the Houston Astros rallied from a two-run deficit for a 4-2 victory over the Cardinals.

Derek Bell doubled -- his third hit of the game -- off Dennis Eckersley (0-1) to start the 10th and Luis Gonzalez was hit by a pitch. Tony Eusebio flied out and Spiers, batting for Russ Johnson, laced a double to right field that cleared the bases.

Billy Wagner (1-0) struck out the side in the ninth to get the win and John Hudek pitched a perfect 10th for his second save. Wagner has 17 strikeouts in 9 2/3 innings this season and has allowed just five hits and two walks.
Eckersley allowed two runs and two hits while retiring just two batters.
In New York, ex-Met Jeff Kent tormented his former club, hitting a two-run homer in the eighth that led the San Francisco Giants to a 3-2 victory and a sweep of the three-game series.

Kent, who strained his neck trying a headfirst slide into third base in the first game of Sunday's doubleheader, belted a 3-2 offering from Greg McMichael over the fence in the left-field corner for the tying and go-ahead runs.
He also drove in a run in the third with an infield single, this time successfully completing a headfirst slide into first.

Rich Rodriguez (2-1) retired all four batters he faced for the win and Rod Beck worked a 1-2-3 ninth for his seventh save. The Giants recorded their first three-game sweep at Shea Stadium for since August 1978.

McMichael (0-1) allowed two runs and two hits in two innings. Starter Dave Mlicki allowed one run and five hits over six-plus innings before leaving with a bruised right shin after being hit by a line drive off the bat of Mark Lewis to start the seventh.
